cms.name: WordPress
cms.technology: PHP / MySQL (database layer); browser-based admin (client layer)
capabilities: Supports themes and plugins (60,000+ free plugins)
Full control over code and hosting
limitations: Security depends heavily on plugins, which must be vetted and kept updated
Requires frequent core/theme/plugin updates and self-managed hosting
Performance can degrade with too many plugins

source.label: Elementor - WordPress site examples of big brands

cms.name: Shopify
cms.support: Supported by Shopify, a proprietary (closed-source) company
cms.technology: Ruby on Rails with Liquid templating; hosted cloud (no self-hosting); JavaScript/React storefronts
capabilities: Hosted e-commerce with payments and POS built in
limitations: Transaction fees unless using Shopify Payments

cms.name: Squarespace
cms.support: Supported by Squarespace, a proprietary (closed-source) company
cms.technology: Closed-source hosted stack; JSON template system; browser-based editor (client layer)
limitations: Can't export a full site to another host

cms.name: Drupal
cms.support: Open Source (GPL), community-supported by the Drupal Association
cms.technology: PHP on the Symfony framework / MySQL or PostgreSQL; Twig templating; browser-based admin
limitations: Fewer themes and modules than WordPress

source.label: Zyxware - 16 organization websites built using Drupal

cms.name: Joomla
cms.technology: PHP / MySQL (MariaDB supported); MVC architecture; browser-based admin
limitations: Smaller extension marketplace and community than WordPress
Harder for beginners than hosted builders
